title: Gurmeet Singh vs Brajesh Rai on 9 June, 2026
full_text: Gurmeet Singh vs Brajesh Rai on 9 June, 2026 IN THE COURT OF Ms. AASTHA SHARMA, LD. JMFC (N.I. Act)-03, SOUTH-EAST DISTRICT, SAKET COURTS COMPLEX: DELHI Gurmeet Singh Vs. Brajesh Rai CC No. 624449/2016 U/S 138 Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 1. CNR number DLSE020021412013 2. Name of the complainant Sh. Gurmeet Singh, S/o Late Sh. Uttam Singh, R/o H. No. 144, Village Jaitpur, P.O. Badarpur, New Delhi - 110044. 3. Name of the accused person(s), parentage Sh. Brajesh Rai, & residential address S/o Sh. Senapati Rai, R/o H. NO. D-44, Jaitpur extension, Part - II, Badarpur, New Delhi - 110044. CC No. 624449/2016 Gurmeet Singh Vs. Brajesh Rai Page 1 of 16 Digitally signed by AASTHA SHARMA AASTHA Date: SHARMA 2026.06.09 16:28:14 +0530 Also at: H. No. 442, Block - O, Sourav Vihar, Jaitpur, Badarpur, New Delhi - 110044. 4. Offence complained of or proved U/s 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 5. Plea of the accused Pleaded not guilty and claimed trial 6. Final Judgment/order Acquittal 7. Date of judgment/order 09.06.2026. Date of Institution : 04.01.2013 Date of Reserving Judgment/Order : 20.05.2026 Date of Pronouncement of Judgment/Order : 09.06.2026. ARGUING COUNSELS: Ld. Counsel for the complainant : Sh. Rajesh Saraswat and Sh. Mahender Kumar Ld. Counsel for the Accused : Sh. Anis Mohd. CC No. 624449/2016 Gurmeet Singh Vs. Brajesh Rai Page 2 of 16 Digitally signed by AASTHA SHARMA AASTHA Date: SHARMA 2026.06.09 16:28:20 +0530 JUDGMENT 1. Vide this judgment, this Court shall dispose of the present complaint filed by the complainant Sh. Gurmeet Singh (hereinafter referred to as "complainant") against Sh. Brajesh Rai (hereinafter referred to as the "accused") under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 read with Section 142 of Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 (hereinafter referred to as " NI Act "). Brief facts of the case: 2. It is the case of the complainant, A. That, the complainant and accused had regular financial transactions and the complainant had advanced a total sum of Rs. 1 crore to the accused partly through his bank account, partly through bank account of the wife of the complainant and partly in cash. That, the accused was paying interest upon aforesaid amount to the complainant @ 24% per annum but after September 2012, the accused stopped paying interest on the aforesaid loan. That, the accused in pursuance of the loan amount issued 5 post dated cheques to discharge his liability, (i) cheque bearing no. 277405 dated 01.11.2012 in the sum of Rs. 10,00,000/- drawn on J&K Bank, Sarita Vihar, New Delhi. (ii) cheque bearing no. 277407 dated 01.11.2012 in the sum of Rs. 80,00,000/- drawn on J&0K Bank, Sarita Vihar, New Delhi. (iii) cheque bearing no. 648322 dated 24.11.2012 in the sum of Rs. 5,00,000/- drawn on ICICI Bank Ltd, Greater Kailash Branch, New Delhi. CC No. 624449/2016 Gurmeet Singh Vs. Brajesh Rai Page 3 of 16 Digitally signed by AASTHA SHARMA AASTHA Date: SHARMA 2026.06.09 16:28:25 +0530 (iv) cheque bearing no. 491425 dated 24.11.2012 in the sum of Rs. 2,50,000/- drawn on Corporation Bank, Sarita Vihar, New Delhi. (v) cheque bearing no. 491427 dated 24.11.2012 in the sum of Rs. 2,50,000/- drawn on Corporation Bank, Sarita Vihar, New Delhi. B. That, the complainant presented cheque bearing no. 648322 dated 24.11.2012 for Rs. 5,00,000/- drawn on ICICI Bank Ltd., Greater Kailash Branch, W-57, Greater Kailash Branch, New Delhi, out of the above in his bank Oriental Bank of Commerce, Jasola, New Delhi, but the cheque was returned unpaid with endorsement "Account Blocked" vide return memo dated 27.11.2012. C. In these circumstances, the complainant got issued a statutory legal demand notice to the accused person through his counsel, dated 30.11.2012, thereby requiring the accused person to pay the amount of the aforesaid cheques within a period of 15 days from the receipt of the said notice. The said notice under Sec. 138 of NI Act was sent to the accused person through Registered AD/Speed Post/Courier at their correct address. That despite service of the above stated notice of demand, the Accused person has deliberately and willfully failed to comply with the said notice of demand and has failed to pay the amount of the aforesaid cheque within the stipulated period of 15 days from the date of receipt of the said notice. Consequently, this case was filed by the complainant against the accused persons, which was within the limitation period as laid down u/s 138 , NI Act. 3. In the pre-summoning evidence, the complainant examined himself on affidavit being Ex. CW1/1 and relied on documents Ex. CW1/A to Ex. CW1/L-2. CC No. 624449/2016 Gurmeet Singh Vs. Brajesh Rai Page 4 of 16 Digitally signed by AASTHA AASTHA SHARMA SHARMA Date: 2026.06.09 16:28:29 +0530 4. Upon prima facie consideration of the pre-summoning evidence, the accused person was summoned. 5. Upon the appearance of the accused, notice under Section 251 CrPC was served upon him on 10.03.2014 to which he pleaded not guilty. The accused stated that him and the complainant were both partners in business and on 23.11.2012, he went to his village and that is when the complainant had misused the cheques in question lying in his office as the complainant was in need of money. 6. CW-1 to CW-5 were examined-in-chief, cross-examined and discharged. Thereby, CE was closed. Accordingly, matter proceeded to the stage of recording the statement of the accused person. 7. Statement of accused no. 4 under Section 313 CrPC read with Section 281 CrPC was recorded wherein the accused opted to lead defence evidence. DW-1 to DW-4 were examined, cross-examined and discharged. Thereafter, DE was closed vide order of this court. 8. Thereafter, the matter was listed for final arguments. After hearing the final arguments from both sides, the matter was reserved for pronouncement of judgment. 9. It is well settled position of law that to constitute an offence under Section 138 , NI Act, the following ingredients are required to be fulfilled: I. drawing of the cheque by a person on an account maintained by him with a banker, CC No. 624449/2016 Gurmeet Singh Vs. Brajesh Rai Page 5 of 16 Digitally signed by AASTHA SHARMA AASTHA Date: SHARMA 2026.06.09 16:28:33 +0530 II. The cheque was issued for payment to another person for discharge in whole/part any debt or liability; III. Cheque has been presented to the bank within a period of six months from the date on which it is drawn or within the period of its validity whichever is earlier. RBI in its notification DBOD.AML BC.No.47/14.01.001/2011-12 has reduced the aforesaid period from 6 months to 3 months. IV. Returning of the cheque unpaid by the drawee bank for want of sufficient funds to the credit of the drawer or any arrangement with the banker to pay the sum covered by the cheque; V. Giving notice in writing to the drawer of the cheque within 30 days of the receipt of information by the payee from the bank regarding the return of the cheque as unpaid demanding payment of the cheque amount; VI. Failure of the drawer to make payment to the payee or the holder in due course of the cheque, of the amount covered by the cheque within 15 days of the receipt of the notice. The offence under Section 138 , NI Act is made out against the drawer of the cheque, only when all the aforementioned ingredients are fulfilled. 10. Analysing all the concerned provisions of law and various pronouncements in this regard, the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Basalingappa v. Mudibasappa [AIR 2019 SC 1983] held that: CC No. 624449/2016 Gurmeet Singh Vs. Brajesh Rai Page 6 of 16 Digitally signed by AASTHA SHARMA AASTHA Date: SHARMA 2026.06.09 16:28:37 +0530 I. Once the execution of cheque is admitted, Section 139 of the Act mandates that a presumption be drawn that the cheque in question was for the discharge of any debt or other liability. II. The presumption under Section 139 is a rebuttable presumption and the onus is on the accused to raise the probable defence. The standard of proof for rebutting the presumption is that of preponderance of probabilities. III. To rebut the presumption, it is open for the accused to rely on evidence led by him or accused can also rely on the materials submitted by the complainant in order to raise a probable defence. Inference of preponderance of probabilities can be drawn not only from the materials brought on record by reference to the circumstances upon which they rely. IV. That it is not necessary for the accused to come in the witness box in support of his defence. Section 139 imposes an evidentiary burden and not a persuasive burden. It is therefore implied that the law regarding the presumption for the offence under Section 138 , NI Act, the presumptions under Section 118(a) and Section 139 have to be compulsorily raised as soon as the execution of cheque by the accused is admitted or proved by the complainant and thereafter the burden is shifted upon the accused to prove otherwise. Appreciation of evidence and marshalling of facts: CC No. 624449/2016 Gurmeet Singh Vs. Brajesh Rai Page 7 of 16 Digitally signed by AASTHA SHARMA AASTHA Date: SHARMA 2026.06.09 16:28:41 +0530 11. Issuance of cheque: The complainant has filed on record the original cheque, i.e., bearing no. 648322 dated 24.11.2012 for Rs. 5,00,000/- drawn on ICICI Bank, Greater Kailash Branch, New Delhi (Ex. CW1/E). In notice under Section 251 CrPC, the accused has admitted that the cheque in dispute belongs to him. It is also not disputed that the cheque in question is not drawn on the account maintained by the accused and it is impliedly admitted therefore that the accused is the drawer of the cheque. Therefore, ingredient number I stands fulfilled in the present case. 12. Presentment and dishonor of cheque: As per the RBI guidelines, it is essential for the cheque in question be to presented within a period of three months from the date on which they are drawn and the same be returned as unpaid by the drawee bank for want of sufficient funds to the credit of the drawer or any arrangement with the banker to pay the sum covered by the cheque. In the case at hand, the cheque in question was returned vide return memo dated 27.11.2012 (Ex. CW1/F) due to the reason "Account Blocked" By implication thereof, the cheque was presented within three months and the same was returned. Therefore, Ingredient number III & IV stand fulfilled in the present case. 13. Legal demand notice and payment by the accused thereof: The legal notice dated 30.11.2012 (Ex. CW1/I) was dispatched on 30.11.2012 vide Speed Post (Ex. CW1/J-1 & Ex. CW1/J-2), i.e., within 30 days of return of the bank memo indicating cheques in question being unpaid. The fact that the legal demand notice has made a clear and unambiguous demand for payment of the cheque in question is not disputed. The accused has not admitted to the receiving of legal demand notice in notice u/s 251 CrPC. However, as per the presumption raised under Section 114 of CC No. 624449/2016 Gurmeet Singh Vs. Brajesh Rai Page 8 of 16 Digitally signed by AASTHA AASTHA SHARMA SHARMA Date: 2026.06.09 16:29:01 +0530 Indian Evidence Act, 1872 and Section 27 of General Clauses Act, if the legal demand notice is sent at the correct address, then the same shall be deemed to have been duly served, as per the precedent laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in C.C. Alavi Haji v. Palapetty Muhammed , (2007) 3 SCC (Cri). The ingredient number V is fulfilled by virtue of giving of legal demand notice within 30 days from the bank return memo. The receipt of legal demand notice by the accused is deemed to be admitted as per the discussion above. 14. Moving on, it is not disputed that the accused has not made the payment of the cheque amount within 15 days of the receipt of legal demand notice. Therefore, ingredient number VI also stands fulfilled in the present case. Presumption under Section 118A read with Section 139 , NI Act 15. The NI Act raises two presumptions in favour of the holder of the cheque, i.e., complainant; firstly, with regard to the issuance of cheque for consideration, as contained in Section 118(a) and secondly, with regard to the fact that the holder of cheque received the same for discharge, in whole or in part, of any debt or other liability, as contained in Section 139 of the Act. These presumptions shall end only when the contrary is proved by the accused, that is, the cheque was not issued for consideration and in discharge of any debt or liability etc. The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in its judgment titled Rangappa Vs. Sri Mohan , (2010) 11 SCC 441 held that a reverse onus clause usually imposes an evidentiary burden and not a persuasive burden and when an accused has to rebut the presumption under Section 139 , the standard of proof for doing so is that of CC No. 624449/2016 Gurmeet Singh Vs. Brajesh Rai Page 9 of 16 Digitally signed by AASTHA SHARMA AASTHA Date: SHARMA 2026.06.09 16:29:05 +0530 "preponderance of probabilities". Therefore, if the accused is able to raise a probable defence which creates doubts about the existence of a legally enforceable debt or liability, the prosecution can fail. It was further held that the accused can rely on the materials submitted by the complainant in order to raise such a defence and it is conceivable that in some cases the accused may not need to adduce evidence of his/her own. Once a probable defence is raised, then the onus is shifted to the complainant to establish that a legally enforceable liability existed in his favour and the burden of proof on the complainant in this case is that of "beyond reasonable doubt." 16. The accused can rebut the presumption as raised under Section 138 , NI Act by: (a) putting forth his defence at the time of framing of notice u/s 251 CrPC; (b) cross-examining the complainant; (c) when statement of accused is recorded u/s 313 CrPC; (d) or by leading defence evidence, thereby demolishing the case of the complainant. Rebuttal of Presumption by Accused as to existence of legally enforceable debt 17. In light of the above discussion, since the accused has admitted to issuance of cheques, admitted the signatures on the cheques and legal notice has also been deemed to be served, what is left to be seen is whether the accused has been able to rebut the presumption against him, i.e., whether the accused is able to raise a CC No. 624449/2016 Gurmeet Singh Vs. Brajesh Rai Page 10 of 16 Digitally signed by AASTHA AASTHA SHARMA SHARMA Date: 2026.06.09 16:29:09 +0530 probable defence which creates doubts about the existence of a legally enforceable debt? 18. In the present case, in order to discharge his initial burden to prove the abovementioned ingredients, the complainant relied upon the affidavit of the complainant being Ex. CW1/1 and placed on record documents mentioned hereinbefore. The case of the complainant is that the accused had issued the cheque in question in discharge of his liability qua the loan of Rs. 1 crore advanced by the complainant to the accused. 19. The primary defence of the accused person is that there was no loan transaction as alleged by the complainant. The amount transferred by the complainant and his family members was for an investment in the partnership business where the accused and the complainant were partners. The accused person has further stated that he has settled the accounts with the complainant qua the partnership and has already paid Rs. 72 lakhs to the complainant. To support and prove his defence, the accused person has produced Ex. CW2/D2 (OSR) (Colly), which are the receipts of payment received by the complainant. At this stage it is pertinent to note that the complainant has admitted the partnership deed Ex. CW2/D1, however he has denied that the accused gave him Rs. 72 lakhs at the time of dissolution of the firm. The complainant has admitted to receiving Rs. 72 lakhs in paragraph 7(c) of reply to the preliminary objections in Ex. CW1/DX3 (OSR). The complainant has not been able to give any satisfactory explanation to the fact of admission of receiving the money as per Ex. CW1/DX3 (OSR). Moreover, Ex. CW2/D2 (OSR) (Colly) has been proved by the testimony of other defence CC No. 624449/2016 Gurmeet Singh Vs. Brajesh Rai Page 11 of 16 Digitally signed by AASTHA SHARMA AASTHA Date: SHARMA 2026.06.09 16:29:17 +0530 witnesses. The Ld. Counsel for the complainant has challenged the veracity of Ex. CW2/D2 (OSR) (Colly), by giving suggestions to the witnesses that the accused has misused the receipts that were lying with him. The complainant in his cross examination dated 27.02.2016 has admitted his signatures on Ex. CW1/D2 (OSR) (Colly), he has stated that the accused has misused the loan documents of Gulshan Finance by cutting the upper part. However, the above explanations do not rebut the fact that the complainant himself has admitted to receiving the amount in Ex. CW1/DX3 (OSR). In lieu of the above discussion and the admission of the complainant, it is right to conclude that the complainant had received Rs. 72 lakhs from the accused person. 20. As per the case of the complainant, he has advanced Rs. 40,75,000/- in cash to the accused person. The Ld. Counsel for the accused person has questioned the financial capacity of the complainant to advance a loan of Rs. 1 crore. The law regarding the financial capacity of the lender is well settled. In cases in which the impugned loan transaction is in cash, the accused can raise a probable defence by questioning the financial capacity of the complainant, and once the said question is raised, the onus shifts on the complainant to prove his financial capacity. In the present case, the complainant has stated that he has advanced loan to the accused person from the consideration received for sale of his agricultural land. At the outset it should be noted that the sale consideration as per Ex. CW1/N is only Rs. 43,95,000/-, however the complainant in his cross examination dated 11.12.2018 has stated that the sale consideration was Rs. 1,05,00,000/- and out of this amount he has advanced loan to the accused only. Further CW4 i.e. Ms. Gurmeet Kaur in her cross examination dated 04.02.2016 has stated that the sale consideration was Rs. 83 lakhs. CC No. 624449/2016 Gurmeet Singh Vs. Brajesh Rai Page 12 of 16 Digitally signed by AASTHA SHARMA AASTHA Date: SHARMA 2026.06.09 16:29:21 +0530 Clearly the sale consideration mentioned in Ex. CW1/N is not the same as claimed by the complainant and CW4. Further, such a huge loan was provided by the complainant to the accused without obtaining any receipt or any other document in this regard and this cannot be equated with the conduct of a prudent man acting in similar circumstances. Similarly, no receipt or ITR was furnished by the complainant to showcase his financial capacity. The complainant in his cross examination dated 27.02.2016 has stated that his monthly income in 2011-12 was Rs. 50,000/- to 60,000/- approximately. In the cross examination dated 11.12.2018 the complainant has stated that one Sh. Manoj used to work in the office of the complainant and he stole Rs. 21 lakhs; he has lodged an FIR also against him. This further raises a doubt on the capacity of the complainant to advance a loan when he has been duped of Rs. 21 lakh. The complainant in his cross examination dated 17.05.2023, has stated that he has advanced a total 3 loans to the accused till date and out of them 2 loans have been returned by the accused person. The complainant has even produced Ex. CW1/X1, which is the receipt dated 05.02.2007 executed for the first loan of Rs. 1 lakh. It is highly improbable that a person who has executed a receipt for a loan of Rs. 1 lakh will advance a loan of Rs. 1 crore to the same person without execution of a single document. This also creates a doubt in the case of the complainant. 21. In Dashratbhai Trikambhai Patel versus Hitesh Mahendrabhai Patel and others Crl.A. No. 1497/2022, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that the cheque that is dishonoured must represent a legally enforceable debt on the date of maturity or presentation. If the drawer of the cheque pays a part or whole of the sum between CC No. 624449/2016 Gurmeet Singh Vs. Brajesh Rai Page 13 of 16 Digitally signed by AASTHA SHARMA AASTHA Date: SHARMA 2026.06.09 16:29:25 +0530 the period when the cheque is drawn and when it is encashed upon maturity, then the legally enforceable debt on the date of maturity would not be the sum represented on the cheque. Even if the case of the complainant is believed to be true, the complainant has failed to show the existing legal liability of the accused. The complainant in his cross examination dated 05.02.2018 has stated that the accused used to pay him Rs. 2,00,000/- in cash as interest and he received the same from June, 2011 to August, 2012. This means that the complainant has received Rs. 2 lakhs for 15 months i.e. Rs. 30 lakhs. However, the complainant has not clarified whether this interest is including the interest of the amount advanced to his family members; because in her cross examination dated 04.02.2016, CW4 has stated that the accused has paid interest 2% per month on Rs. 19.90 lakh which is the amount given by her to the accused, from May, 2011 to August, 2012 i.e. for 17 months and the interest paid comes out to be Rs. 6,76,600/- (17 months x Rs. 39,800). If the alleged principal loan amount was Rs. 1,00,00,000/- (1 crore) on 01.06.2011, and interest was charged at Rs. 2,00,000/- per month (2% monthly) up to 01.11.2012 (date of the cheques in question), then: ● Period: 17 months (from 01.06.2011 to 01.11.2012) ● Monthly interest: Rs. 2,00,000/- Total interest = Rs. 2,00,000/- × 17 = Rs. 34,00,000/- Therefore: ● Principal: ₹1,00,00,000/- CC No. 624449/2016 Gurmeet Singh Vs. Brajesh Rai Page 14 of 16 Digitally signed by AASTHA SHARMA AASTHA Date: SHARMA 2026.06.09 16:29:30 +0530 ● Total Interest: ₹34,00,000/- ● Total Amount Payable/Return: ₹1,34,00,00/- If the interest paid by the accused as per the statement of CW1 and CW4 is combined, it becomes Rs. 30,00,000/- + Rs. 6,76,600/- i.e. 36,76,600/-. As discussed above the complainant has also admitted to receiving Rs. 72,00,000/-. Therefore, it is not possible to decide the actual liability of the accused, if any, on the date of presentation of the cheque. The onus shifted on the complainant to show the liability of the accused on the date of presentation of the cheque when during the cross examination it came to light that the accused had already paid some interest, which the complainant failed to discharge. 22. In view of the aforesaid findings and analysis, this court has arrived at an irresistible conclusion that the accused has been able to cast a shadow of reasonable doubt upon the case of the complainant by rebutting the mandatory presumption resting in its favour and by several inconsistencies in the version of the complainant. Once the accused had created a probable defence as to the legally enforceable liability, the onus shifted on the complainant to prove the existence of legally enforceable liability of the accused, as on the date of the drawal or presentation of the impugned cheques, which has not been fulfilled by the complainant in the present case by bringing any other document to prove the financial transaction between the complainant and the accused. Since this basic ingredient which is pivotal to attract liability under Section 138 NI Act has not been proved by the complainant, accordingly, no offence of dishonour of the impugned cheque under the said Section is made out. CC No. 624449/2016 Gurmeet Singh Vs. Brajesh Rai Page 15 of 16 Digitally signed by AASTHA SHARMA AASTHA Date: SHARMA 2026.06.09 16:29:34 +0530 23. In light of the discussion above, ingredient no. II has not been fulfilled in the present case. Conclusion: 24. In view of the aforesaid discussion, the accused Brajesh Rai is hereby acquitted of the offence punishable under Section 138 , Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881. PRONOUNCED IN THE OPEN COURT TODAY ON 09th June, 2026.
